candidate.title: EC-seq
candidate.scope: Excision circle sequencing (EC-seq), at the assigned Illumina poster schematic scope: RAG-mediated antigen-receptor recombination, its chromosomal coding-junction and extrachromosomal signal-circle co-products, and the circle-derived read-pair mapping readout. The biological reaction is illustrated as a V2–J3 event, not a restriction to those segments. Paper-supported enrichment, library, and sequencing interfaces explain the compressed circle-to-readout arrow. Adjacent DSB-Seq, GUIDE-seq, and Bubble-Seq rows are outside the assigned EC-seq target; IR-seq discussed in the paper is a separate, unshown method.

states.label: Excision-circle-enriched DNA extract
features: Paper-supported material interface between biological circle generation and library construction; enrichment is not drawn as a separate poster block.
The primary EC-seq implementation uses plasmid-type purification and RecBCD/T5 exonuclease treatment.

The paper states that extraction may favor small circles because larger circular species are more susceptible to exonuclease digestion and loss during silica-column purification; this is not an unbiased census of all excision circles.

states.label: Reference-mapped read pairs identifying excision-circle junctions
features: The poster shows pairs aligned across a V/J reference segment track.
For the classical V–J event drawn here, fragments spanning the circle signal junction yield RF pairs with reversed relative mapping orientation; other fragments also give standard pairs.

The RF pair spans the circle closure: its reverse read maps upstream and faces away from its forward read on the unrearranged reference. Their reference separation reflects the excised circle length rather than the library insert length.

Mapped junction flanks reveal the recombination partners represented by the library. Recovery and mapping constrain this observation; it does not itself establish expression of a productive antigen receptor.

The primary paper also recovers nonclassical circles bearing hybrid coding-to-signal junctions. Thus the illustrated classical signal junction is an example, not a claim that every EC-seq circle has that junction type.

operations.label: Lymphocyte-specific recombination activating gene (RAG) recombinase, bound genome
operations.description: RAG binds antigen-receptor DNA at recombination signal sequences; the initially unbound locus becomes RAG-bound. This is biological target generation, not an instruction to add RAG during library preparation.
operations.mechanism: Binding and juxtaposition of RSS-flanked segments by the RAG complex.

operations.label: Synapsis, cleavage and coding end hairpin formation
operations.description: RAG-bound V and J sites are brought together and cleaved, converting the intact locus into a synaptic intermediate with hair-pinned coding ends and signal ends.
operations.mechanism: RAG-mediated double-stranded cleavage at RSS sites with covalent coding-end hairpins.
operations.information_effect: Recombination partners are brought into a common molecular intermediate.

operations.label: Resolved genomic coding junction; Liberated excision circle with resolved signal junction
operations.description: Resolve the cleaved intermediate into two linked products: ligated chromosomal coding ends and a circular excised DNA product with a signal junction.
operations.mechanism: Coding hairpins are reopened and ends processed before ligation; the remaining signal ends are ligated with little modification.
operations.information_effect: The chromosome retains a coding-segment join, while the excision circle carries the signal-end join and excised interval.

operations.label: Align read pairs to reference genome
operations.description: Map EC-library read pairs to the unrearranged reference locus and identify junction-spanning pairs by their relative mapping positions and orientation.
operations.information_effect: In the classical V–J example, RF mapping identifies a fragment spanning the signal junction and links its two reference flanks, revealing excision-circle recombination partners. Standard mapped pairs describe other fragments and do not themselves identify a circle junction. RF orientation establishes a closure-spanning architecture; the paper also reports hybrid coding-to-signal circle junctions, so the signal-to-signal interpretation is restricted to the depicted classical example.

method_scopes.rationale: All operations describe the EC-seq schematic or the paper-supported interface needed to interpret its circle-to-read-pair transition. RAG binding, cleavage and junction resolution generate the biological analyte in lymphocytes. The genomic coding product is a co-product, not a separate IR-seq library branch. No alternatives are named within the EC-seq row. The primary paper supports recovery of nonclassical hybrid circles within EC-seq, but those findings do not create another target workflow or replace the classical example drawn here.
